market.definition: Paid appointment-reminder software (text and email) bought by independent, non-corporate veterinary clinics in the United States, standalone or as an add-on plan.
exclusions: Reminders bundled free inside practice-management software
market.interpretation: Read as software sold to clinics, priced per clinic, not messaging volume sold to pet owners.

bottom_line: The US market for paid appointment-reminder software at independent veterinary clinics was about $30M in 2025 (range $14M to $50M), from 40,000 clinics, 25% paying for a reminder tool and $3,000 a year per clinic [S1][S2][S3]. TAM, if every independent clinic paid, is about $120M. A realistic SOM for a new entrant is about $3M over three to five years, which is inference. Confidence is medium: two inputs are sourced, but the price is one vendor's.

published_estimates.title: US veterinary practice software market
published_estimates.scope: All practice-management software including billing, records and imaging; reminders are one feature. Not the same market.

estimate_gap: The only published figure covers all practice software, which is about 40 times wider than reminder tools alone, so it is context, not a competing estimate.

bottom_up.formula: independent clinics x adoption rate x annual spend per paying clinic

inputs.name: Independent US veterinary clinics, end of 2025
Share of clinics paying for a reminder tool
inputs.reasoning: Survey of 1,200 clinics reports 25%; the range allows for sample error and survey bias toward software users.

inputs.name: Annual spend per paying clinic
inputs.reasoning: One vendor's published plan is $250 a month; other vendors may charge 20% less or more.

tam.method: All 40,000 independent clinics x annual spend per clinic ($2,400 to $3,600).

sam.method: About half of TAM: clinics that use cloud practice software and could connect a reminder tool. The 50% (40% to 60%) is a judgment.

som.method: 5% of SAM (range 5% to 7.5%), a plausible share for a new entrant against the incumbent in three to five years. Judgment, no comparable share was found.

reconciliation: The bottom-up result ($30M of current spend) is a quarter of TAM ($120M) because only 25% of clinics pay today. The published $1.3B figure covers a much wider market and does not check either number.

drivers.point: Only 25% of independent clinics pay for a reminder tool, so adoption has room to grow.

sources.title: Independent veterinary clinics in the US, 2025

report_markdown:
## Bottom line
The US market for paid appointment-reminder software at independent veterinary clinics was about $30M in 2025 (range $14M to $50M): 40,000 clinics, 25% paying, $3,000 a year [S1][S2][S3]. TAM is about $120M. A new entrant's SOM is about $3M, which is inference. Confidence is medium: the price is one vendor's.

## Market definition
Paid reminder software bought by independent US veterinary clinics, vendor-revenue basis, 2025. Excludes corporate chains and reminders bundled free into practice software. NAICS 541940.

## Published estimates
| Publisher | Data year | Value | Scope | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PetPractice Insights | 2025 | USD 1.3 billion | all practice software, much wider | summary only [S4] |

## Bottom-up build
Formula: clinics x adoption x spend.

| Input | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Clinics | 40,000 | fact [S1] |
| Adoption | 25% (15% to 35%) | fact [S2] |
| Spend per clinic | $3,000 (2,400 to 3,600) | inference [S3] |

40,000 x 0.25 = 10,000 clinics; 10,000 x $3,000 = $30M.

## TAM / SAM / SOM
- TAM $120M (calculation): every clinic pays [S1][S3].
- SAM $60M (inference): about half can connect a tool.
- SOM $3M by 2030 (inference): 5% of SAM.

## Sensitivity
| Case | Adoption | Spend | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low | 15% | $2,400 | $14.4M |
| Base | 25% | $3,000 | $30M |
| High | 35% | $3,600 | $50.4M |

## Caveats and gaps
One vendor's price. Paywalled report seen as a summary. SAM and SOM are judgments. One player profiled.
